unsupported_claims: Advances in language modeling are expected to help network representation learning by providing stronger pretrained text encoders.
They help by modeling node, edge, and graph semantics from textual attributes, descriptions, and surrounding context.
Improved language models can supply richer embeddings and more transferable semantic knowledge for graphs.
Graph modeling can feed back into language modeling by injecting explicit relational and structural information such as entity links, dependency structure, and broader network context.
This would help language models move beyond purely sequential text.
Language models would thereby learn representations that are more context-aware and structurally informed.
rationale: The paper only supports the narrower claim that advances in language modeling may generate improved latent representations for networks, and that modeling observable graphs may improve modeling of unobservable language graphs. The answer adds many specific mechanisms and examples (pretrained text encoders, textual attributes, entity links, dependency structure, context-aware structural learning) that are not stated or implied by the source.
